scope: Proposition 4.13 (Links within one sphere cover) of the manuscript “Abelian covers, Gale correspondences, and the Hodge conjecture for powers” (preprints/Abelian-covers-Gale-correspondences-and-the-Hodge-conjecture-for-powers-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 032 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3467c8077855a568), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 28-29. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose two non-toric character spaces Wχ, Wχ′ are supported by the same simple Hodge Lie ideal. They have the same dimension n and standard derived representations equivalent up to duality. (i) If n ≥ 3, then χ′ = χ or χ−1. The inverse character is identified by the polarization with the polarized dual. If the standard group is symplectic, the character has order two and the space is mixed at every scalar translate. 28 (ii) If n = 2, one can choose either Wχ or its polarized dual as model so that an equivalence of its derived representation with Wχ′ respects the Hodge circle at every scalar translate.
